title: Try This Eye Trick: See Colors That Are Not There
summary:
Here is a fun trick. Stare at a colorful picture for 30 to 60 seconds. Then look at a plain white wall or paper. You will see a ghost-like copy of the picture in different colors! This is called an afterimage.

Your eyes see color with special cells called cone cells. There are three kinds, often called red, green and blue. When you look at something red, your red cones tell your brain, "That is red!"

When red, green and blue light mix, they make white. So when you look at something white, all three kinds of cones work together.

But cone cells can get tired. If you stare at a red circle for a long time, your red cones take a break. Then, when you look at white, only your green and blue cones work. So you see a blue-green circle!

After a few seconds, your red cones wake up again, and the afterimage goes away. Try it with different colors.
why_it_matters: It is a fun way to learn how your own eyes and brain work together.
